newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to stay cautious in coming days.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to stay cautious in coming days.

text.p: Belgian shares are expected to maintain gains in coming days provided the dollar keeps up its bull run and Wall Street stays in positive territory, traders said on Monday.
But they said volumes were likely to remain thin as institutionals are reluctant to jump back into the market, fearing an imminent hike in U.S. interest rates.
The Bel-20 closed up 1.69 percent at 2,115.85, with a thin 2.3 billion francs volume of Belgian shares traded.
"A lot of institutionals are not yet ready to invest, they're afraid of what might happen to rates," a trader said.
"I'd be surprised if we get high volumes this week. There's a lack of buyers in the markets, and more good news is needed before cash will be poured into the market again," another trader said.
"We're in a wait-and-see mood," one trader said.
Attention was on retailer Delhaize after U.S. brokerages downgraded their recommendations for shares in Delhaize's U.S. Food Lion unit.
This was sparked by Food Lion's announcement that first quarter 1997 growth had been slowed by its acquisition last year of U.S. Kash 'n Karry chain.
Delhaize traded in a 1,760 to 1,685 francs range before closing down 0.29 percent at 1,725 francs, with a hefty 670 million Belgian francs volume of the share traded.
International shipper CMB climbed 4.78 percent to 2,630 francs, with traders putting it down to the strong dollar.
Cement maker CBR, which closed up 3.66 percent at 3,395 francs, and steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, which ended up 2.38 percent at 21,475 francs, were also buoyed by the bullish dollar.
